sentences.text: He would further rely on the order passed by this very bench in Special Civil Application No.794 of 2023 dated 14.03.2023.

The said order reads as under:
"1. We have heard Mr. Kunal Vyas, learned advocate with Mr. Devarsh Trivedi,
learned advocate for Gandhi Law Associates for the petitioner, Ms. Archana Amin,
learned advocate for respondents no. 2 & 3 and Ms. Shrunjal Shah, learned Assistant Government Pleader for the State respondents.
The affidavit-in- reply filed by respondents no. 2 and 3 is taken C/SCA/902/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/03/2023 on record.
2. Rule returnable forthwith.
Learned advocates for the respondents waive service of notice of rule.
With the consent of the learned advocates for the parties, matter is taken up for final hearing today.

3. In this petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has prayed for a writ of mandamus commanding the respondent authority to recompute the amount of compensation awarded to the petitioner under Award No.
05/2015/Kukarwada/Bharuch dated 22.03.2016, 02/2016/Kukarwada/Bharuch dated 15.02.2017, 01/2016/Dahegam/Bharuch dated 15.02.2017 and 09/2016/Kukarwada/Bharuch dated 16.06.2017 by applying multiplication Factor-2 and the recompute other statutory benefits as provided under the provisions of Section 26 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 read with the First Schedule.

4. Reliance is placed on an oral judgement of a coordinate Bench of this court rendered in the case of the Dhiraj Ambalal Patel vs. State of Gujarat [2020 (1) GLR 752].
5.

6. Considering the awards in question and the survey numbers so stated in the awards for which recomputation is sought and in light of the statement made by Ms.
Shrunjal Shah, learned AGP that admittedly in case of the awards in question the multiplying factor-2 is applicable, the petition is allowed.

The respondents are directed to recalculate compensation and other statutory benefits as prayed for by applying the multiplying Factor - 2 in light of the decision in case of Dhiraj Ambalal Patel (supra) after verifying the details of each land.
The entire exercise shall be completed within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order of this court.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In this petition, under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the petitioner has prayed to issue a writ of mandamus to recompute the amount of compensation under the award n o .
The respondents are directed to recalculate compensation and other statutory benefits as prayed for by applying the multiplying Factor - 2 in light of the decision in case of Dhiraj Ambalal Patel (supra) after verifying the details of each land.
The entire exercise shall be completed within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order of this court.
5. In view of the above order passed and considering the awards in question and the survey numbers so stated in the awards for which recomputation is sought and in light of the statement made by Ms.
Shah , learned AGP that admittedly in case of the awards in question the multiplying factor-2 is applicable, the petition is allowed.
The respondents are directed to recalculate compensation and other statutory benefits as prayed for by applying the multiplying Factor - 2 C/SCA/902/2023 ORDER DATED: 21/03/2023 in light of the decision in case of Dhiraj Ambalal Patel (supra) after verifying the details of each land.
The entire exercise shall be completed within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of the writ of the order of this court.
Rule is made absolute.
